name: Custom sub-drop: automate a sine from ~80 Hz down to ~20 Hz
goal: Design original sub/bass drops without sample packs by generating a mono sine (test tone or sine osc), automating frequency from about 80 Hz (or key-matched) down to about 20 Hz over a chosen length (half-bar to multi-bar), bypassing the generator outside that window, and optionally adding bass-harmonic saturation.

source.title: How to make custom bass drops / sub drops in Cubase (tutorial)

prerequisites: Sine oscillator or test-tone generator with automatable frequency

inputs.name: start_hz
inputs.description: Starting frequency (transcript examples ~70–80 Hz, or 160 for absurd; ideally match song key)

inputs.name: length_bars
inputs.description: Drop length in bars (half, 1, or elongated)

outputs.name: sub_drop_clip
outputs.description: Exported mono sub-drop ready to drop on a hit point

constraints: Portable signal-flow recipe for Web Audio / Traveler-inspired / any hybrid synth with comparable modules; not affiliated with any vendor.
Do not copy proprietary factory preset banks, wavetable file names, or sample packs; use original/free waves or generic shapes.
Steps and numeric values are grounded only in the YouTube Show-transcript text; approximate where the speaker gestured without stating a number.
Keep the generator bypassed/muted outside the drop so a constant test tone does not leak into the mix.
Check mono compatibility and speaker/headphone bass response; very low endings may be felt more than heard.

steps.action: Create a mono track and insert a sine test-tone generator (or a sine-only oscillator). Name the track as a sub-drop layer.
steps.expect: Clean mono sine available for automation

steps.action: Pick a start frequency near 80 Hz (or look up the Hz for your song's root); set end near 20 Hz for a deep trailer-style drop.
steps.expect: Start tone matches key/feel; end is sub-rumble

steps.action: Draw frequency automation from start_hz to end_hz across the chosen length (e.g. 1 bar). Elongate or shorten the automation for brutal long drops vs fast stabs.
steps.expect: Smooth downward glide over the window

steps.action: Automate bypass/mute so the generator is only active during the drop window.
steps.expect: Silence outside the hit; no stuck 80 Hz drone

steps.action: Optional: add bass-harmonic exciters/saturation (e.g. 'max bass'-style) if you want audible upper harmonics; verify on a spectrum that harmonics appear only when desired. Export several lengths/keys into a personal drop folder.
steps.expect: Harmonic version reads on small speakers; dry version stays clean sub

verification: Frequency lane falls from start_hz to end_hz across the intended bars
No tone outside the automated window
Drop lands on the arrangement hit without clicks (short fades if needed)
